title: A framework-level exception thrown from handler code is caught, mapped to the wire, and never leaks a raw stack trace
iWant: a framework-level exception to produce a mapped wire response, not a raw stack trace or a truncated connection
soThat: callers can act on the error without inspecting server logs and no internal detail leaks

acceptanceCriteria.description: A handler that throws produces a wire response written by ADR-1703's transport mapping; the response body carries the fields the transport blueprint's errorEnvelope ADR requires (no raw stack, no PII, code present, message present); the server does not truncate the connection.
acceptanceCriteria.then: the response arrives cleanly with the mapped wire body, and no raw stack trace or internal path appears in the body

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given a handler that throws a JavaScript Error with a stack trace containing a filesystem path, when the framework-level boundary catches the exception, then the wire response body carries no stack, no filesystem path substring, and no file:// URL; the response's error envelope is populated only through ADR-1703's transport mapping. The check drives a fixture endpoint that throws a synthetic Error with a stack containing /Users/, /home/ and file:// prefixes and inspects the response body substrings.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a fixture endpoint whose handler throws an Error carrying a stack with filesystem paths and file:// URLs
acceptanceCriteria.when: the framework-level boundary catches the exception and writes the wire response
acceptanceCriteria.then: the response body carries no stack, no /Users/, no /home/ and no file:// substring; only the transport envelope fields populate

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given a handler that throws a plain object literal (not an Error instance) and one that throws a primitive (string, number), when the framework-level boundary catches, then the constructed record's category defaults to `unknown` when no code pattern maps, message defaults to a controlled placeholder (never the raw thrown value), and the wire response follows ADR-1703's transport mapping the same as for an Error. The check drives fixture endpoints that throw `{foo: 1}` and `'string thrown'` and inspects the emitted record and the wire response.
acceptanceCriteria.given: fixture endpoints that throw non-Error values (a plain object and a bare string)
acceptanceCriteria.then: the record's category resolves to `unknown` (no code pattern), the message is a controlled placeholder (not the raw thrown value), and the wire response is written via ADR-1703's transport mapping

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given a handler that throws AFTER the response body has already begun streaming to the client (headers flushed, partial body written), when the framework-level boundary observes the exception, then the connection is closed without attempting to rewrite the wire response, exactly one error record emits through the logging companion at error level naming the streaming-in-progress condition, and the boundary contract records the emitted record with category `unknown` unless the throwing site supplied one.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a handler that has flushed headers and started streaming when an exception fires
acceptanceCriteria.when: the framework-level boundary observes the mid-stream exception
acceptanceCriteria.then: the connection is closed cleanly, one record emits through the logging companion at error level naming the streaming-in-progress condition, and no further bytes are written to the wire
